1	# Open Relief
2	
3	Predict district-level **FEWS NET IPC phase three months ahead** from six months of
4	monthly food-security, shipping, conflict, rainfall and food-price histories. Deterioration
5	(an increase of at least one IPC phase) is a secondary analysis. Official OpenTSLM is the
6	primary model; simple classical models are comparison baselines.
7	
8	Local data preparation and native TimeNet connectors are implemented. Annotation has been
9	tested with a small live pilot; **full annotation runs later on this machine**, followed
10	by fine-tuning on a separate CUDA machine. See [current status](docs/STATUS.md) for measured
11	results and remaining work. No OpenTSLM improvement has been measured yet.
12	
13	## Current dataset
14	
15	| Partition | Rule | Examples |
16	|---|---|---:|
17	| Training | Target plus assumed release lag available by December 2022 | 9,065 |
18	| Validation | January–July 2023 cutoffs, labels available by July 2023 | 2,503 |
19	| Test | August–December 2023 cutoffs, exact target at cutoff +3 months | 2,230 |
20	
21	Labels that cross the training or validation freeze are purged. The eligible validation
22	cutoffs therefore end in March 2023. Training spans 16 countries; test has 14, with no
23	eligible Yemen or Ethiopia examples. These are country-imbalanced retrospective samples,
24	not independent crisis events. Six complete monthly FCS/rCSI observations remain required.
25	
26	There are **21 monthly channels**, with an availability mask for each at model input:
27	
28	- FCS/rCSI normalized indices, and the requested plain `month_of_year` integers 1–12.
29	- Last known IPC phase and assessment age, reconstructed as of each historical month.
30	- Four PortWatch measures, ACLED events/fatalities, CHIRPS rainfall, WFP staple price.
31	- One- and three-month price percentage changes and FCS/rCSI differences, trailing
32	  three-month conflict events, and cargo imports relative to the previous three months.
33	
34	Derived series use only the existing six-point window. Early entries without enough
35	history remain null, as do ratios with nonpositive denominators. No new downloads were
36	needed for these features. Source prefixes are retained so an ablation removes both a
37	source and its derived features. IPC history expires after six months without an assessment.
38	
39	All non-calendar series are scaled to [-1,1] within each input window, with original scale
40	statistics and units retained in text. Calendar scaling is fixed from 1–12; there are no
41	sine/cosine channels. The official patch-size-4 collator pads six observations to eight
42	positions. Padding is a model operation, not extra observed months.
43	
44	## Local setup and rebuilding
45	
46	Use Python 3.12 for the complete TimeNet workflow:
47	
48	```sh
49	python3.12 -m venv .venv
50	.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-local.lock.txt
51	.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
52	bash scripts/rebuild_local.sh
53	```
54	
55	`rebuild_local.sh` uses the already downloaded monthly artifacts and original HFID CSV.
56	It makes no API calls. To acquire fresh data, follow
57	[the separate acquisition project](open-relief-data/README.md). A fresh acquisition produces
58	three all-country monthly files; supply those three to `open_relief.enrich` instead of
59	mixing them with overlapping country-extension files from this workspace.
60	
61	Inputs, objective targets, manifests and annotations are separate artifacts. Dataset
62	loading verifies checksums. `reports/dataset-validation.json` records sample counts,
63	country coverage, channel missingness and temporal checks.
64	
65	## Annotation: test now, full run later here
66	
67	Keep the official OpenAI API key in `.env`, following `.env.example`; never include it in
68	a handoff. The selected model is `gpt-5.6-terra`. It receives training records and their
69	objective future phase, using strict JSON output. Recalled context and inference are
70	separated from observed evidence; retrieved evidence is disabled unless actually supplied.
71	Annotations are retrospective supervision and never become inference inputs.
72	
73	```sh
74	# Small diverse live test; not the full training set.
75	bash scripts/annotate_local.sh pilot
76	
77	# Run later, on this machine, when ready to prepare all fine-tuning supervision.
78	bash scripts/annotate_local.sh full
79	
80	# Verify full coverage before transferring it to the training machine.
81	.venv/bin/python -m open_relief.validate artifacts/multimodal \
82	  --annotations artifacts/annotations-training.jsonl --require-complete-annotations \
83	  --output reports/pretraining-validation.json
84	```
85	
86	The full command selects all 9,065 training examples, uses eight workers, and stops before
87	a conservative $185 cache-wide accounting ceiling. It may finish fewer examples if that
88	ceiling is reached; check the output manifest. Keep `artifacts/annotation-cache` between
89	runs. Exact requests reuse cached responses, including after validation fixes. Budget
90	reservations persist for ambiguous API failures; automatic API retries are disabled.
91	Only one annotation process may own the cache at a time. Do not delete the cache to reset
92	spend accounting. Other API projects and old pre-ledger attempts are outside this ledger;
93	the margin below the user's $200 budget is intentional.
94	
95	Validated schema and unchanged labels do not guarantee every explanation is factually
96	correct. Review numeric claims, assessment dates, national/local scope and causal language
97	on a sample before treating rationales as high-quality supervision. `confidence` is an
98	annotation-quality judgment, not calibrated forecast probability.
99	
100	## GPU fine-tuning later
101	
102	The runner imports official OpenTSLM at commit
103	`2968f4b891baab4307f7e9d0043e87677b593a30`. It defaults to the official Llama 3.2 1B TSQA
104	SP checkpoint and records resolved checkpoint/backbone revisions and hashes. SP is the
105	initial practical choice, not an empirically established winner. The runner also supports
106	the official corresponding Flamingo checkpoint.
107	
108	On a Linux CUDA machine, with Hugging Face access to Llama 3.2 1B configured:
109	
110	```sh
111	bash scripts/setup_gpu.sh
112	bash scripts/train_gpu.sh artifacts/gpu-run
113	```
114	
115	The training script requires complete annotations. It first evaluates pretrained OpenTSLM,
116	then fine-tunes and evaluates the same 256 deterministically selected test IDs. Use a fresh
117	output directory per run. The direct CLI accepts `--eval-limit 100000` for the full held-out
118	partitions and `--checkpoint OpenTSLM/llama-3.2-1b-tsqa-flamingo` for the alternative.
119	For a phase-only comparison, invoke `python -m open_relief.gpu artifacts/multimodal` without
120	`--annotations`; the rationale target is then empty and explanation learning is not tested.
121	
122	Training uses official architecture, collator, loss, LoRA and checkpoint methods, with
123	batch size one and gradient accumulation eight, maximum ten epochs, and patience three.
124	Validation uses phase JSON prefix loss, excluding retrospective rationale text. Outputs
125	include pretrained/fine-tuned raw predictions, country metrics, losses, checkpoint and a
126	before/after table. Generation validity is scored separately. GPU dependencies are pinned
127	from inspected upstream versions; CUDA execution remains to be tested on that machine.
128	
129	## Evaluation, plots and transfer
130	
131	```sh
132	.venv/bin/python -m open_relief.evaluate artifacts/multimodal
133	.venv/bin/python -m open_relief.ablation artifacts/multimodal --split validation
134	.venv/bin/python -m open_relief.demo artifacts/multimodal --output artifacts/demo-final
135	.venv/bin/python scripts/package_handoff.py
136	```
137	
138	After training, pass `--predictions artifacts/gpu-run/fine_tuned.jsonl` to the demo command.
139	Without predictions, the two plots explicitly show input case studies with GPU forecasts
140	pending. They are selected by historical worsening, not prediction correctness.
141	The transfer archive includes code, prepared data and available annotations; it excludes
142	`.env`, virtual environments, raw download caches and obsolete pilots. Run packaging again
143	after the full annotation job to include its training JSONL and manifest.
144	
145	## Material limitations
146	
147	Historical release timestamps and revisions are unavailable: HFID, PortWatch, ACLED and
148	WFP use an assumed one-month lag; CHIRPS uses two. This is a retrospective research
149	benchmark, not proof of real-time forecasting performance. Country-level external signals
150	are shared by districts; country-average rainfall is not district exposure. Shipping is
151	not food-specific, food prices depend on changing market composition, and FCS/rCSI
152	normalization direction is undocumented. Price coverage is about 73%, shipping 79%,
153	conflict 100%, rainfall 83% after lag masking. No missing observation becomes a real zero.
154	
155	Classical ablations measure association rather than causation. Do not equate a three-month
156	forecast horizon with demonstrated warning lead time or claim additional data improve
157	forecasts until held-out experiments support it. Source terms and provenance are in
158	[the source inventory](docs/SOURCES.md) and acquisition manifests.
